title: Conjecture 1 (Zhang, Liu, and Wang)
statement_text: Every graph with maximum degree $\Delta \geq 3$ and no isolated edge has an AVD-colouring with $\Delta + 2$ colours.
context_text: Zhang, Liu, and Wang (2002) conjectured this optimal bound on the number of colours needed in an adjacent vertex distinguishing edge colouring. The condition $\Delta \geq 3$ is required because $C_5$ needs five colours and is the only connected graph known to require more than $\Delta + 2$ colours. Prior to this paper, Hatami proved the conjecture holds up to an additive constant by showing $\Delta + 300$ colours suffice for $\Delta > 10^{20}$.
paper_contribution: Proves that every graph with maximum degree $\Delta \geq \Delta_0$ (for some explicit constant $\Delta_0$) and no isolated edge has an AVD-colouring with at most $\Delta + 19$ colours, substantially improving Hatami's $\Delta + 300$ bound via the entropy compression method.

title: Open Problem: $\Delta + O(1)$ bound for neighbour sum distinguishing colourings
statement_text: It is an intriguing open problem whether a $\Delta + O(1)$ bound holds on the number of colours required for a neighbour sum distinguishing edge colouring.
context_text: Graphs have no parallel edges, and colourings are edge colourings. For a proper edge colouring $c$ of $G$ and a vertex $u$, $S_c(u)$ is the set of colours on the edges incident to $u$; $c$ is adjacent vertex distinguishing (an AVD-colouring) if $S_c(u)\ne S_c(v)$ for every edge $uv$ (a constraint only when $u,v$ have the same degree). Zhang, Liu and Wang conjectured in 2002 that every graph with maximum degree $\Delta\ge3$ and no isolated edge has an AVD-colouring with $\Delta+2$ colours ($C_5$ needs five colours). Hatami proved, with the Local Lemma, that $\Delta+300$ colours suffice when $\Delta>10^{20}$, and the authors improve this to $\Delta+19$ for large enough $\Delta$ using entropy compression. A neighbour sum distinguishing colouring is a proper edge colouring with positive integer colours such that for every edge $uv$, the sum of the colours of the edges incident to $u$ differs from the sum of the colours of the edges incident to $v$; it is in particular an AVD-colouring. Flandrin et al. conjectured that every graph with no isolated edge and maximum degree $\Delta\ge3$ has such a colouring with colours in $\{1,\dots,\Delta+2\}$, a strengthening of the Zhang–Liu–Wang conjecture. The best known asymptotic bound on the number of colours, due to Przybyło, is $\Delta+O(\Delta^{1/2})$. The authors note that neither Hatami's proof for AVD-colourings nor their own entropy compression argument seems adaptable to this setting.

title: Informal Conjecture: probabilistic methods insufficient for the $\Delta+2$ bound
statement_text: One could suspect, as we do, that probabilistic methods such as the Local Lemma or entropy compression will probably not be enough on their own to prove the $\Delta+2$ bound from the conjecture of Zhang, Liu and Wang (every graph with maximum degree $\Delta\geq 3$ and no isolated edge has an AVD-colouring with $\Delta+2$ colours), assuming the conjecture is true.
context_text: Graphs have no parallel edges, and colourings are edge colourings. For a proper edge colouring $c$ of $G$ and a vertex $u$, $S_c(u)$ is the set of colours on the edges incident to $u$; $c$ is adjacent vertex distinguishing (an AVD-colouring) if $S_c(u)\ne S_c(v)$ for every edge $uv$ (a constraint only when $u,v$ have the same degree). Zhang, Liu and Wang conjectured in 2002 that every graph with maximum degree $\Delta\ge3$ and no isolated edge has an AVD-colouring with $\Delta+2$ colours ($C_5$ needs five colours). Hatami proved, with the Local Lemma, that $\Delta+300$ colours suffice when $\Delta>10^{20}$, and the authors improve this to $\Delta+19$ for large enough $\Delta$ using entropy compression. The authors find it remarkable that probabilistic techniques come so close to the conjectured bound and see this as extra supporting evidence for the conjecture, but suspect that such methods alone cannot reach $\Delta+2$ since, intuitively, some extra colours are bound to be 'wasted' in any random process. This is a methodological belief rather than a precise mathematical statement.
